column4: Prior full affirmative solution credited to Robert Šámal, Cycle-Continuous Mappings—Order Structure, Journal of Graph Theory 85(1), 56–73 (2017), DOI 10.1002/jgt.22047, first online 12 June 2016. The original finite-graph question uses inverse images of the full binary cycle space, including disconnected even edge sets. Actual essential proof inspected in arXiv:1212.6909v1, Theorem 1.3 and Corollary 3.5; the path family consists of finite simple cubic connected bridgeless graphs. This independent AI-only review reconstructs the two primary-figure Blanuša blocks, supplies new exact 54 edge-deletion flow witnesses and cut/matching checks, and verifies path-specific localization plus no-collapse/no-folding without importing general tree localization or small-snark classification. The journal DOI and publisher antichain abstract are authenticated; the journal mathematical body was inaccessible and is not claimed inspected. Earlier same-author/same-title proceedings DOI 10.1007/978-88-7642-475-5_81 (2013) has an authenticated explicit antichain abstract but an uninspected body; arXiv and publication-family aliases are not separate project solutions. Historical raw audit inputs were unavailable and not reproduced. No external human review, formal certification, priority/novelty, stronger cyclic-connectivity family or countable-poset universality claim is made.
